questions.title: Check if Number is Prime
questions.problem_statement: Write an efficient algorithm to check whether a given integer N is a prime number.
questions.hint: Check divisibility up to square root of N: for (int i = 2; i * i <= N; i++).

questions.title: Find Fibonacci Term Iteratively & Recursively
questions.problem_statement: Write a function to generate the N-th Fibonacci number. Compare the iterative O(N) time & O(1) space approach against simple recursion.
questions.hint: Iterative approach uses two variables (a=0, b=1) updated in a loop up to N.

questions.title: Java Access Modifiers (public, private, protected, default)
questions.problem_statement: Explain the four access modifiers in Java: public, private, protected, and default (package-private), detailing their visibility across packages.
questions.hint: Private is class-only; Default is package-only; Protected is package + subclasses; Public is accessible everywhere.

questions.title: Constructors in Java & Default Constructor Behavior
questions.problem_statement: What is a Constructor in Java? Explain default constructor vs parameterized constructor and Constructor Overloading.
questions.hint: If no constructor is defined in a class, the Java compiler automatically inserts an explicit no-argument default constructor.

questions.title: SQL SELECT DISTINCT & ORDER BY Query
questions.problem_statement: Write a SQL query to retrieve distinct job designations from an Employee table, sorted in alphabetical ascending order.
questions.hint: Use SELECT DISTINCT designation FROM Employee ORDER BY designation ASC.

questions.title: DBMS Relational Model & Foreign Key Reference Integrity
questions.problem_statement: Explain Referential Integrity in DBMS. What happens when you attempt to delete a parent row referenced by child Foreign Keys?
questions.hint: Requires ON DELETE CASCADE, ON DELETE SET NULL, or throws a foreign key constraint violation error.

questions.title: Operating Systems Deadlock Conditions
questions.problem_statement: List the four necessary Coffman conditions required for a Deadlock to occur in an operating system.
questions.hint: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait.

questions.title: Computer Networks IP Address Classes & Port Numbers
questions.problem_statement: Differentiate between IPv4 Class A, Class B, and Class C addresses. What are well-known port numbers for HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, and SSH?
questions.hint: HTTP=80, HTTPS=443, FTP=21, SSH=22.

questions.title: Average Calculation & New Entry Impact
questions.problem_statement: The average weight of 24 students in a class is 45 kg. If the teacher's weight is included, the average weight increases by 1 kg. What is the teacher's weight?
questions.hint: Teacher's weight = New Average + (Old Count * Increase) = 46 + (24 * 1) = 70 kg.

questions.title: Percentages & Discount Calculation
questions.problem_statement: A laptop originally priced at $800 is offered at successive discounts of 10% and 5%. What is the final selling price?
questions.hint: Price after 10% discount = 800 * 0.90 = $720. Price after 5% discount = 720 * 0.95 = $684.

questions.title: Time & Work Pipes and Cisterns
questions.problem_statement: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours and Pipe B can empty the full tank in 12 hours. If both pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.hint: Combined rate = 1/6 - 1/12 = 1/12 per hour. Time required = 12 hours.

questions.title: Number Series Pattern Completion
questions.problem_statement: Complete the series: 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, ?
questions.hint: Each term is doubled (multiplied by 2).

questions.title: Logical Reasoning Coding Decoding
questions.problem_statement: If 'WIPRO' is coded as 'XJQSP', how is 'JAVA' coded in the same scheme?
questions.hint: Pattern: Each letter is incremented by +1 in alphabetical order.

questions.title: Tell Me About Yourself
questions.problem_statement: Tell me about yourself, your background, education, and interest in software development.
questions.hint: Keep it clear and enthusiastic: focus on degree, key technical skills, project participation, and readiness to learn.

questions.title: Why Do You Want to Join Wipro?
questions.problem_statement: Why do you want to join Wipro?
questions.hint: Mention Wipro's global repute, inclusive corporate culture, training programs (like Elite/Turbo), and strong technology footprint.

questions.title: Why Should We Hire You?
questions.problem_statement: Why should Wipro select you over other candidates?
questions.hint: Highlight your strong fundamental understanding, quick learning agility, positive attitude, and commitment to project success.

questions.title: Strengths and Weaknesses
questions.problem_statement: What are your core strengths and an area of weakness you are actively working to improve?
questions.hint: Share a practical strength (e.g. perseverance, analytical thinking) and a genuine weakness with your proactive improvement plan.

questions.title: Challenging Situation Handled
questions.problem_statement: Describe a challenging situation or obstacle you faced in your academics or project and how you resolved it.
questions.hint: Use STAR format: explain the obstacle, your initiative, team coordination, and positive outcome.

questions.title: Willingness to Relocate
questions.problem_statement: Are you comfortable relocating to different Wipro office locations across India or working in shifts?
questions.hint: Confirm flexibility and eagerness for broader industry exposure.

questions.title: Five-Year Career Goals
questions.problem_statement: Where do you see yourself professionally five years from now at Wipro?
questions.hint: Express intent to develop deep technical domain expertise, take on module responsibility, and contribute to client projects.
